domain: Why did ancient tree-ring records of long-dead volcanic eruptions become a crisis for the standard chronology of the Bronze Age Mediterranean, and what does the argument over 'radiocarbon plateaus' really reveal about historical time itself?
topic: Why did ancient tree-ring records of long-dead volcanic eruptions become a crisis for the standard chronology of the Bronze Age Mediterranean, and what does the argument over 'radiocarbon plateaus' really reveal about historical time itself?

source.title: Astrophysicists Puzzle Over Webb’s New Universe

movement.gist: Pose the puzzle plainly: radiocarbon dating of a volcanic destruction layer (e.g. Thera) places it a century or more earlier than the pottery and textual synchronisms with Egypt suggest; the straightforward answer is that one method must simply be recalibrated against the other until they converge.

Show that decades of recalibration, tree-ring 'wiggle-matching,' and refined statistical modeling have narrowed but not closed the gap, and worse, sharpened resolution has revealed that the discrepancy is structurally stubborn — full convergence keeps receding rather than arriving, suggesting the mismatch isn't a rounding error waiting to be fixed.

Reframe: the real difficulty isn't which measurement is more accurate but that radiocarbon time and historical time are answering different questions — one tracks atmospheric carbon-14 fluctuation, the other tracks human record-keeping and political memory, and the field has been asking a single timeline to do the work of two incommensurable ones.

Leave open what a chronology should even be for once you accept it's not a single timeline: is the goal to synchronize physical and cultural time, or to make peace with two chronologies that answer different needs — the essay ends without adjudicating this, since evidence only shows the old goal was wrong, not what the right one is.

primary.axis: whether the discrepancy between radiocarbon dates and archaeological/textual dates for events like the Thera eruption is a measurement problem or an interpretive one
poles: the gap can be closed by better calibration and more precise samples
the gap reflects an irreducible mismatch between two different kinds of 'when'

secondary.axis: whether chronology is a neutral scaffold for history or an argument-laden construction that determines which historical narratives are even askable

tension_system.interaction: the primary tension is initially fought as a technical dispute, but the secondary tension shows the technical dispute was always downstream of a prior choice about what chronology is for
